name: Serval
summary: Serval builds an AI-native system of record and automation platform for IT and operational teams.
overview: Serval provides enterprise automation and service-management software designed to let operational teams automate work from natural-language prompts. The company announced a $75 million Series B led by Sequoia in December 2025 at a $1 billion valuation.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Serval raised $75 million in Series B funding at a reported $1 billion valuation.

bull_case: AI-native automation can consolidate workflows across IT, HR, finance, and legal if Serval proves it can displace legacy service-management systems.
bear_case: Incumbents have deeply embedded systems of record, and enterprise automation demands reliability, governance, and lengthy sales cycles.
latest_round: December 2025 Series B: $75M at a reported $1B valuation
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: An AI-native automation and service-management platform for enterprise operations.
company: Serval is building an AI-native system of record for IT teams and the operational functions they support. The platform aims to automate work end to end through a natural-language interface rather than through traditional workflow configuration alone.
In December 2025, Serval announced a $75 million Series B led by Sequoia at a $1 billion valuation. The company said the financing brought total capital raised to $127 million since August.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Serval is a direct test of whether AI can become the operating layer for internal enterprise work, not merely an assistive feature. Its traction matters to the broader service-management and automation software market.

changed.text: Serval announced a $75M Series B led by Sequoia at a $1B valuation.

takeaways: The Series B established a $1B valuation and $127M cumulative funding figure.
Expansion beyond IT is central to the platform's growth thesis.
Service-management incumbents and execution risk remain material.
